- Every GitHub workflow display name starts with exactly one tag — [TEST], [PROD], [DB] or [REPO]; [PROD] marks workflows that can touch the PROD canister set (promotion, push delivery and the PROD setup, audit and funding workflows), and renamed workflows retain their paths. Why: the Actions list must state which canister set a run can touch.
- Group 2 owner opening runs only through the manual protected GitHub environment with the existing deploy key, explicit confirmation, exact revision/modules/subnets/controllers and live consensus configuration checks; reports exclude unrelated environment values and never authorize general opening. Why: readiness evidence is separate from the owner's signed limited grant.
- Group 2 upgrades use only its checked thirteen-service inventory and staged recipe artifacts, preserve Motoko memory/settings/photo-key attestation, and persist/read back each intent on the dedicated receipts branch; ambiguous calls never replay automatically. Why: existing group data and routing must survive runner interruptions, and upgrades must not grant admission.
- Group stop controls use the existing signed governor through a protected administrator workflow and revision-CAS stop-only API; never require owner UUID approvals or grant opening, and retain existing assignments. Why: halting new placements must not interrupt current clubs or widen admission.
- General-opening settings, snapshot and stop runners resolve fixed repository files relative to their module URL, not the working directory. Why: GitHub runs opening from frontend and stop from root.
- Opening checks and snapshots resolve the existing CI delivery identity or matching recorded approval, never the first queue grant. Why: missing approval values or unrelated workers cannot prove delivery wiring.
- PROD connection audits use a fixed provisioned inventory and exact infrastructure-reader allowlist in a manual protected workflow; consensus read methods may be updates but setters/deployments/business reads are excluded; calls go through the pinned @icp-sdk/core agent with typed IDL (never parsed icp-cli output) and the result table is printed to the job log as well as the summary. Why: the existing encrypted key can verify links without activating routing or repointing DEV, and CLI output formats broke decoding.
- PROD group readiness is separate from connection health: require bounded complete independent group/placement inventories, identity/router binding and configuration-revision approval; unknown group IDs need independent review and all audits/proposals deny opening. Why: installed services, zero expected links and a fresh unpinned identity cannot establish DEV-equivalent groups or authorize lifecycle release.
- PROD base registration uses a standalone closed-only runner, exact certified inventory/revision hash, protected deployment concurrency and remotely acknowledged intent receipts on a separate branch; pending calls stop without replay. Persist safe allowlisted failure-stage reports and loaded/acknowledged receipts even on failures; never print raw agent/API errors. Why: metadata registration must preserve existing canisters and remain separate from identity lifecycle release, paid g2 creation and admission opening, while failed runs remain diagnosable without leaking credentials.
- Evidence JSON (evidenceText) converts principals/bigints from the raw holder value, never the replacer argument; an interrupted pending-readback registration finishes only via reconcile-readback, which uses the read-only actor and writes just the final receipt. Why: Principal.toJSON runs before replacers and caused a false PROD readback mismatch after a correct registration.
- PROD notification keys are minted only in protected CI with a durable pre-mint intent and authenticated passphrase-encrypted receipt; closed g2 resolves only the verified PROD principal in memory, never publishes plaintext seeds or enables delivery. Why: browser-only handover must not rotate existing keys, reuse DEV identities or change working Supabase push.
- PROD setup receipts (g2 registration, settings promotion) are read only from the default receipts branch via githubJournal's default; never pass another branch. Why: a wrong-branch read returned no g2 record and stopped the live settings repair.
- TEST gallery post-upgrade wiring uses gallery-authority-repair-policy for both metadata-to-club/Vault and the reverse club-to-metadata link, with per-assignment pending/completed receipts. Why: an outbound-only assignment leaves the trusted notification relay refusing uploads.
- TEST push provisioning uses the isolated manual existing-key transfer; delivery requires atomic generation/attempt receipts and authoritative runner fencing, never a variable alone. Why: hosted secrets and persistent read/write journals cannot prevent duplicate sends.
- PROD push delivery requires an explicit recipient allowlist (PROD_ICP_PUSH_RECIPIENTS_JSON), decrypts the stored encrypted worker key in memory against the recorded principal, and settles non-listed or >30-minute-old alerts without sending. Why: staged native rollout to approved accounts must never flood phones or reach other users.
- All-member native push is toggled only by the manual governor workflow prod-native-push-rollout.yml with an exact confirmation phrase, the queue's currently bound sender and readback. Why: the switch must stay separate from code upgrades.
